INTRO07: All right. Files ready, team ready... where's my phone?
You said, 'Nobody move anything.' We took you seriously.
Do we get detective badges for finding it, or is that still a household chore?
CASEWALL12: I was thinking my best theories could go across the top. In big letters.
How big are the facts allowed to be?
Mine can go underneath Dilo's. Then mine will look more reasonable.
Could I have that little corner? I want to write 'We don't know yet.'
Leave her plenty of room. That's usually our biggest category.
Everyone step back a little. I'd like our new detective to see the wall before we fill it with ourselves.
CASE01: The envelope came from inside the Academy. No courier. That gives us somewhere to start.
I've already got a secret tunnel and a minivan. We could start there.
You've arranged transport before finding a single clue?
He drew the minivan first. It's got all our names on the seats.
Then I want a window. I can watch for the evidence on the way.
CASE02: Look how neatly the Cup's sitting there. That is exactly how I put things back when I hope nobody asks where they've been.
We know. You line your shoes up after you've used someone's good scissors.
That happened once. And this Cup is much tidier than my shoes.
Well, I'm glad we've cleared the scissors up. The Cup still has a blank return sheet.
And no pockets. We should probably ask someone who was in the room.
CASE03: I've found a sparkle on the trophy shelf. I'm calling it Inspector Glitter.
Has Inspector Glitter found any of our ten differences?
Not yet. It likes that shelf too much to look anywhere else.
I could do that job. Stand somewhere shiny and look important.
You'd want a chair by lunchtime. Pass me the other photo.
CASE04: I'll watch the evidence box. Alio, you can patrol the tents.
That's generous. You get to sit down while he does all the walking.
Someone has to stay with the box. I'm prepared to make that sacrifice.
I'll find out who was with Pixel. They might actually have something to tell us.
Can I make my report sitting down, or is that a senior detective skill?
Sit beside your brother. I'll patrol. Apparently it takes two of you to stop a sealed box going anywhere.
CASE05: Six symbols. One locker. Detective, shall we see which of us gets it first?
If the Detective solves it, are you going to say you were just about to?
Only if I was. Which I might be. It's important to keep that possibility open.
I'll leave a little space beside the answer for 'Dilo was nearly there.'
What if the locker beats both of you? Does it get a badge?
No. It already knows the answer. That's a very unfair advantage.
THREAD34: Four matching marks, and still no explanation. Could the printer send a nice ordinary answer for once?
You'd turn it over to look for the puzzle on the back.
I'd settle for a name. My notes say 'the thing from the thing.' I knew what I meant when I wrote it.
Bring them to the archive with me. We can look for proper names while Dilo checks the backs of things.
CASE06: I'd already drawn the dragon. Now I've got a perfectly good dragon and a case about a spoon.
You could give it some soup.
That works. It can be a dragon who cooks.
I'm interested again. Does it breathe fire into the pan, or is that why it needs the spoon?
I was trying to help Nini finish a drawing. I seem to have started a cookbook.
Leave me a page. I've burned enough dinners to contribute.
Grandma! You're supposed to be helping with the real history.
CASE07: Alio, was that the third cupboard or the fourth? I'm starting to recognize the brooms.
Fourth. I checked behind the coats as well.
That moon costume wouldn't fit behind the coats. It barely fits through a door.
Then we've ruled out four cupboards. And all those coats.
Splendid. Let's leave before I start calling the brooms by name.
CASE08: My shortest route gets us there in almost no time. I even drew it in one stroke.
It also gets us to a locked door. What happens to all that time you saved?
Would you like to reconsider here, or after we've all followed you there?
Here, please. I know his reconsidering face. I'd rather see it sitting down.
CASE09: You stopped halfway through saying something. Do you know that mark?
I remember something about it. I want to check before I let you all run off with my memory.
I'll get the records. You can guard Alio while I'm gone.
While we're checking memories, I distinctly remember being promised cake on this investigation.
You promised yourself cake. Quite loudly. Nobody had a chance to agree.
Then I need a better witness. Mine keeps agreeing with Grandma.
CASE10: Two teams claiming one rover. I could keep it here while we sort this out.
I know how to look after a rover. I could even fix that cable.
Dilo, you haven't looked at either ownership sheet. You've already found room for it next to your chair.
Fine. Sheets first. But if anyone needs a temporary rover sitter, I'm still available.
CASE11: Your phone has been living beside the oat bar.
Can I put that in the bag report? Right beside 'Always know where your equipment is.'
You would not. Pass me my source. I haven't had breakfast.
CASE12: For the record: where did you hear those four words?
It's asking for a cracker, Dilo.
I heard. I've written it down three times. I was hoping we'd get to the password.
It thinks you're taking its order.
Right. I'll ask the handler. First witness who's made me feel like a slow waiter.
CASE13: My fox theory has one weakness. I'm trying to work around it.
Exactly. Where does a fox keep a camera?
It needs a little strap. Here, I'll draw one around its neck.
Thank you. Someone has finally taken the equipment problem seriously.
Lovely. Now I want to see the fox. This is why I shouldn't sit next to you two.
CASE14: Somebody sounds very sure about a journey that doesn't seem to fit.
Maybe they've mixed up two moments. I've done that.
So have I. I was absolutely certain I'd packed lunch once. Three books. Not a sandwich in sight.
I remember. You kept checking the bag, as if lunch might be in a different chapter.
Three books? Surely one of them had something to eat in it.
A magnificent feast. I read it while Mom gave me half her sandwich.
CASE15: Next trip, big readable name tags. On every backpack.
I was going to suggest satellite tracking. We could find a bag anywhere on Earth.
With a tag, I can find mine without asking you to charge anything.
Fine. One for each bag. And a little one for your phone, since we're solving family problems.
CASE16: If it rains on our next case, I'm standing under that hat.
Ask first. There may be a grandmother under it.
She used to make me carry it in a separate bag. My sandwiches traveled underneath.
And arrived in perfect condition. You're welcome.
So Alio's not wrong. We could all fit under there.
You may visit. No one is moving in.
CASE17: Helmet on. Ready for the railway investigation.
We're in the ticket hall. The biggest danger so far is you turning around with that backpack.
I've been giving you plenty of warning.
Yes. 'Coming through' is why I'm standing over here with the tickets.
Did he pack anything besides the helmet?
Oh, yes. A very small sandwich. He knows what takes priority.
CASE18: How's your watch taking the news that it's wrong?
Quietly. With dignity. I'm proud of it.
I'm getting there. I've crossed my old times out, haven't I?
You have. I'll check the new ones with you. We can use my watch while yours enjoys being dignified.
CASE19: I was going to say 'digital ghost.'
I'm checking the scanner first. The ghost can wait outside.
You see, now you've made it harder for me to tease you. I had a whole speech ready.
You could lend the ghost a book while it waits.
A paper one. I'm not giving it the Wi-Fi password.
CASE20: That paint smear looks like a very worried pear. See the eyebrows?
I'd rather see who moved the panel. Before you give every splash a name.
Just the pear. It's called Pear.
Easy to remember. Does Pear have an alibi?
CASE21: Leave them just there. We can still see the torn edges.
I only meant to catch it.
I know. Come around here. I need someone to check the joins with me.
We'll put it in a sleeve when it fits. Keep the writing where we can see it.
It feels familiar. I'd like to find another sample before I say more.
I'll check this edge. You take the next one, Detective.
CASE22: I can tell the three cases apart now. That one was on the left.
Before you walked around the table, or after?
Ah. I had a system until you asked that.
I like the labels. They stay on the same case when I walk around it.
Let's use those. I don't want to solve this again every time Alio changes seats.
CASE23: The arcade scoreboard has challenged me personally.
I've got the wristband file. Come on. I'll let you tell me how easily you could beat it on the way.
I could. Easily. You're not allowed to count that as me playing, though.
CASE24: Yes. I want to get a proper look at the prints before I say anything else.
Both of you? I should get a photograph. Nobody at home will believe me.
Footprints first. Put my good behavior next to you finding your phone. I'd like the family album to be fair.
CASE25: Everyone who touched this parcel was helping. It must be exhausting to be that well looked after.
Let's give it a rest. Nobody move it until we know where it belongs.
I'll stay with it. Alio, if you're about to help, put your hands in your pockets.
I was going to get us some cookies. Difficult now.
Hands out, then. That's the first delivery here with a clear destination.
THREAD120: Fourteen selected maps. I knew we'd need all that careful filing.
I kept mine because the stack looked impressive. I've been showing people.
That explains why you asked if the librarian was coming round.
Let him show it off. He's usually showing me something he hasn't finished yet.
He can show them my elbow. It's been holding this corner down for ten minutes.
CASE26: We've been looking at where everyone stood. Now it's the rooms with nobody in them.
Nobody's been very patient. Hasn't interrupted once.
Luli, you once explained a footnote all the way through dinner. Nobody didn't get a word in then, either.
I enjoyed that footnote. But I would like to hear what we've missed.
CASE27: Clean hands, please. And no folding the old map to make room for your elbows.
May I point? I've got a very clean finger and nowhere else to put my excitement.
Above the sleeve. Go on. I want to see what you've noticed.
All those cases, and he's finally been trusted with one finger.
I trust the rest of him too. I just prefer it farther from my map.
CASE28: I've put my tunnel theory on a separate card. With a proper heading. It looks quite convincing.
How much evidence is on the card?
I'd like a card. I've put that into several very organized plans.
Make it two. I used to call mine 'experience.'
CASE29: That's a lot of map. Slide the folders over. Let's give our Detective some room.
Take your time. I'll stay at this end so it doesn't curl up on you.
I can be quiet for one map. If that helps.
It does. I'll save anything worth teasing you about until afterwards.
There. All of us here, and space to think. Begin when you're ready.
CASE30: Case Wall ready? Credential too? Then the panel's yours, Detective.
And the victory noise is mine. I've been saving a good one.
Keep it in your head until the door opens.
Mine's in there too. It's getting very crowded.
Go on. You've brought us this far. We're right behind you.
